analysis.title: Central Banks Keep Buying, Everyone Else Is Selling: Goldman's 2027 Gold Playbook
key_insights: Spot gold touched $3,830 in early trading, the lowest since October 2025 and roughly $300 below its level a month earlier. The article cites a rising dollar and expectations of another Fed rate hike next month.

Goldman cut its end-2027 gold forecast to $4,650/toz from $4,800 in its 2027 precious metals outlook. The $4,800 figure was itself cut from $5,400 eleven days earlier. It adds an end-2028 target of $5,600/toz. The article notes Goldman's targets have tracked spot almost one for one.

Goldman's thesis is that 2027 resembles 2022. A rising Fed policy rate weighs on private investor demand, while structural central bank buying keeps a bid under gold. It expects near-term downside risk and elevated volatility, then gains to $4,650 by end-2027.

Goldman's economists expect a second 25bp Fed hike in December and a third in March 2027. They expect four 25bp cuts between November 2027 and September 2028, taking the funds rate to 3.25-3.5%. One 25bp cut is worth only about 60 tonnes of ETF demand spread over six months.

Goldman's two downside paths: four Fed hikes with a higher terminal rate gives $4,585 at end-2027. A full unwind of ETF holdings above the level implied by rates alone, about 300 tonnes of selling, gives $4,265. The article computes that even this bear case is about 11% above spot of roughly $3,850.

Tactical risks: COMEX speculative positioning is at the 45th percentile. Higher oil prices could trigger more systematic CTA selling. A sharp equity drawdown tied to AI cycle uncertainty could drag gold lower first as margin calls force investors to raise cash. Nasdaq futures were down another 1.2% on the day.

The Market Ear flagged $3,900 as the line in the sand for gold, with next support near $3,400, and noted systematic shorts were already stretched. The article says $3,900 has now been crossed. Heraeus says a 25bp December hike is fully priced and core inflation is running at 0.3% a month.

Goldman explains why gold did not rally on 2026 inflation. It says the source of inflation matters. Institutional credibility shocks like the 1970s lift gold. Supply shocks like Russia's 2022 gas cut see the disrupted commodity outperform, while gold typically underperforms initially as tighter policy and higher yields hit ETF demand and margin liquidations hit. It places the 2026 Hormuz shock in the second regime.

Goldman's positioning advice is split. For CTAs and macro funds, the next 3-6 months may remain challenging, with long positions difficult to hold. For longer-horizon investors, the current correction may offer a more attractive entry point.

The structural bull case assumes central banks buy 60 tonnes a month through 2026-28, against a pre-2022 average of 17 tonnes. The latest nowcast was soft at 31 tonnes in September, with the three-month pace down to 51 tonnes from 85. Goldman calls this a normal pause after a violent price move.

Bank of England custody of central bank gold rose 82 tonnes in September, more than implied UK net imports (17 tonnes) or NY Fed custody (0 tonnes) explain. Goldman reads this as London OTC purchases not captured in its nowcast, so official buying may be larger than the data show.

The PBoC holds an estimated 11.8% of reserves in gold, against roughly 80% for the US, Germany, France and Italy and a global average above 20%. At about 20 tonnes a month, China would take roughly three years to reach a 20% share. Goldman says its desired allocation could ultimately exceed 20%, because larger gold reserves help RMB internationalization.

Central bank selling risk is limited. Turkey is an outlier with gold above 60% of FX reserves. Its 129-tonne drop was partly explained by gold swaps and reserves have since rebounded. Gold is 4% of reserves in the UAE, 8% in Saudi Arabia, 5% in Oman and about 24% in Qatar, and with dollar pegs Gulf FX intervention is more likely through Treasury liquidation than gold sales.

Developed-market reserve holders are debating where to store gold rather than whether to own it, with France and the Netherlands reportedly moving gold away from New York. Goldman reads this as reinforcing the case for retaining rather than selling gold.

Silver's record above $120/toz in January came from tariff-driven metal flows into the US, drained London stocks, then Fed cuts and debasement-trade inflows. Price sensitivity to 1,000 tonnes of weekly net demand rose to about 7% from a typical 2% during the squeeze. Goldman does not expect a repeat in 2027 because Fed hikes should suppress ETF demand.

Goldman expects gold to outperform silver in 2027 until the Fed returns to easing, because silver has no central bank bid. It says this undermines the buy-silver-on-a-high-gold/silver-ratio trade. The article counters that silver specs are very short, which raises squeeze risk.

Goldman sees outright Section 232 tariffs on platinum and palladium as unlikely, but the threat keeps pulling inventories into the US and draining liquidity elsewhere. It expects more volatility but not necessarily higher prices. European BEV sales (+66% y/y in August) weigh on platinum, while US hybrid sales (+27% y/y in Q3) give palladium some cover.

The article's author disputes the timing. Goldman has the Fed hiking into March and not cutting until November 2027. The author expects the Fed to ease sooner, which would pull forward the return of Western ETF buyers, and doubts gold stays near $4,650.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term downside risk and volatility while the Fed hikes, then gains to $4,650/toz by end-2027 and $5,600 by end-2028 on central bank buying and a return of ETF demand once the Fed cuts.
No central bank bid, Fed hikes suppress ETF demand, and the 2025/26 squeeze is not expected to repeat. Goldman expects gold to outperform silver in 2027.
Tariff threats add volatility without necessarily raising prices. European BEV growth hits platinum and US hybrid growth supports palladium.

trade_ideas.description: CTAs and macro funds avoid or reduce long gold positions over the next 3-6 months

trade_ideas.description: Avoid buying silver on a high gold/silver ratio
trade_ideas.rationale: Private flows into both metals move in tandem, and gold is decoupled by central bank buying that silver lacks, so Goldman expects gold to outperform silver in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Silver specs are very short and a squeeze could occur regardless of fundamentals.

tension_points.bull_case: Central banks keep buying about 60 tonnes a month, Goldman sees gold at $4,650 by end-2027 and $5,600 by end-2028, and the current correction may be an attractive entry for longer-horizon money. The article's author expects the Fed to ease sooner than Goldman, pulling ETF buyers back earlier.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed hikes in December and March weigh on rate-sensitive ETF demand. Goldman's downside paths are $4,585 (four hikes) and $4,265 (300 tonnes of ETF selling), CTAs face tight drawdown limits, and equity or AI drawdowns could force margin-related liquidations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Spot holding below the $3,900 line in the sand with $3,400 next support, or a full ETF unwind of about 300 tonnes taking gold to $4,265 by end-2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Silver specs have hardly ever been this short, and lopsided positioning tends to end in a violent squeeze whatever the fundamentals say.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman sees no repeat of the 2025/26 squeeze because Fed hikes suppress ETF demand and silver has no central bank bid, so gold should outglitter silver in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed return to easing would bring back ETF demand and end the case for gold outperforming silver.
